questions.q: Conservation of electric charge states that
options: the total charge of an isolated system remains constant
charge can be destroyed when two bodies touch
charge is lost when a body is earthed and cannot be recovered
questions.explanation: Charge can move from one body to another but is neither created nor destroyed overall.

questions.q: The SI unit of the permittivity of free space ε0 is
questions.explanation: From F = q1q2/(4πε0r²), ε0 has units C²/(N m²).

questions.q: The force between two point charges is F. If one charge is doubled and the distance between them is halved, the force becomes
questions.explanation: F is proportional to q1q2/r², so the change is 2 × (1/(1/2)²) = 2 × 4 = 8 times.

questions.q: A short dipole has dipole moment 2 × 10^-8 C m. The electric field on its axis at a distance of 1 m (large compared with its length) is (1/4πε0 = 9 × 10^9 N m²/C²)
A point charge q is placed at one corner of a cube. The electric flux through a face that does not touch that corner is
questions.explanation: Eight such cubes would surround the charge, so each carries q/8ε0 in total; this is shared equally by the three faces away from the corner: q/24ε0 each.

questions.q: A small sphere of mass 10 g and charge 1 μC hangs from a thread in a horizontal uniform electric field of 10^5 N/C. Taking g = 10 m/s², the thread makes an angle with the vertical of
questions.explanation: qE = 10^-6 × 10^5 = 0.1 N and mg = 0.1 N, so tanθ = qE/mg = 1 and θ = 45°.

questions.q: A metal sphere has 5 × 10^10 excess electrons. Find its charge (e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C).
keyPoints: = 8 × 10^-9 C, negative because of excess electrons
questions.explanation: Excess electrons give a negative net charge.

questions.q: A uniformly charged ring of radius 0.3 m carries a charge of 10 nC. Find the electric field on its axis at 0.4 m from the centre (k = 9 × 10^9 N m²/C²).
questions.answer: 288 N/C along the axis, away from the ring.
questions.explanation: Components perpendicular to the axis cancel, leaving only the axial field.

questions.q: One farad is equal to
questions.explanation: C = Q/V, so 1 F = 1 coulomb per volt.

questions.q: Inside a charged conducting sphere the electric potential is
options: constant and equal to its value at the surface
questions.explanation: The field inside is zero, so no work is needed to move a charge and V is the same as on the surface.

questions.q: A potential difference of 400 V is applied across two parallel plates 2 cm apart. The electric field between them is
Capacitors of 1 μF, 2 μF and 3 μF are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. The total charge stored is
questions.explanation: C = 6 μF, so Q = CV = 6 × 12 = 72 μC.

questions.q: A capacitor is charged from a battery through a resistor. The fraction of the energy supplied by the battery that is finally stored in the capacitor is
questions.explanation: The battery supplies QV, the capacitor stores ½QV, and the other half is dissipated as heat in the resistor.

questions.q: Two conducting spheres of radii 5 cm and 10 cm are far apart and are joined by a thin wire. The ratio of the charges on them, q1 : q2, is
questions.explanation: They reach the same potential, so q/R is the same and q1 : q2 = R1 : R2 = 1 : 2.

questions.q: An air capacitor has capacitance 40 pF. What is its capacitance when a dielectric of dielectric constant 5 fills the space between its plates?
questions.explanation: The dielectric multiplies the capacitance by K.

questions.q: Capacitors of 3 μF and 6 μF are connected in series across a 90 V supply. Find the charge, the potential difference across each and the total stored energy.
questions.answer: Charge = 180 μC on each; potential differences 60 V (3 μF) and 30 V (6 μF); total energy = 8.1 × 10^-3 J.
questions.explanation: In series the smaller capacitor carries the larger share of the voltage.

questions.q: The resistance of a uniform wire is
options: inversely proportional to its length and its area
directly proportional to its length and inversely proportional to its area
directly proportional to its length and its area
inversely proportional to its length and directly proportional to its area
questions.explanation: R = ρl/A.

questions.q: The material used for a fuse wire should have
questions.explanation: It must melt quickly when the current exceeds the safe value and break the circuit.

questions.q: A current of 2 A flows through a 4 Ω resistor. The power dissipated is
A material has resistivity 2 × 10^-6 Ω m. Its conductivity is
A 12 V battery of negligible internal resistance is joined to a 6 Ω resistor in series with a parallel combination of 6 Ω and 3 Ω resistors. The current through the 3 Ω resistor is
questions.explanation: Parallel part = 2 Ω, total = 8 Ω, I = 1.5 A, and the voltage across the parallel part is 3 V, so the 3 Ω resistor carries 1 A.

questions.q: Resistors R and 2R are connected in parallel across a battery. The ratio of the power dissipated in R to that in 2R is
questions.explanation: In parallel the voltage is the same and P = V²/R, so the smaller resistor dissipates twice as much.

questions.q: Why are alloys such as manganin and constantan used to make standard resistors?
questions.answer: They have a high resistivity and a very small temperature coefficient of resistance, so their resistance stays almost constant when the temperature changes.
questions.explanation: A stable resistance is needed for standards and measuring instruments.

questions.q: Estimate the relaxation time of conduction electrons in copper of resistivity 1.7 × 10^-8 Ω m and electron density 8.5 × 10^28 m^-3 (m = 9.1 × 10^-31 kg, e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C).
questions.explanation: The result is of the order of the average time between electron collisions.

questions.q: The magnetic field lines around a long straight current-carrying wire are
questions.explanation: By the right-hand thumb rule the field circles the wire.

questions.q: A radial magnetic field is used in a moving coil galvanometer so that
options: the deflection is proportional to the current
questions.explanation: With a radial field the torque on the coil is independent of its angle, so the deflection is directly proportional to current.

questions.q: A charge of 2 μC moves at 5 × 10^5 m/s at 30° to a magnetic field of 0.2 T. The force on it is
Which statement about ideal measuring instruments is correct?
options: Both an ammeter and a voltmeter have low resistance
An ammeter has high resistance and a voltmeter has low resistance
An ammeter has low resistance and is connected in series; a voltmeter has high resistance and is connected in parallel
questions.explanation: An ammeter must not change the current and a voltmeter must not draw current from the circuit.

questions.q: Two concentric coplanar circular loops of radii 10 cm and 20 cm each carry 5 A in opposite senses. The magnetic field at the common centre is (μ0 = 4π × 10^-7 T m/A)
questions.explanation: B1 = μ0I/2R1 = 3.14 × 10^-5 T and B2 = 1.57 × 10^-5 T in opposite directions, so the net field is 1.57 × 10^-5 T.

questions.q: A rectangular current loop is placed in a uniform magnetic field. The loop experiences
options: zero net force, but possibly a non-zero torque
a non-zero net force and zero torque
a net force and a torque always
neither a force nor a torque in any orientation
questions.explanation: Forces on opposite sides are equal and opposite, so the net force is zero; they can form a couple unless the loop is aligned with the field.

questions.q: State the Biot-Savart law for the magnetic field due to a current element.
questions.answer: The magnetic field dB at a point due to a current element I dl is proportional to I, dl and the sine of the angle between dl and the line joining the element to the point, and inversely proportional to the square of the distance: dB = (μ0/4π) I dl sinθ/r².
questions.explanation: The direction is perpendicular to both dl and the position vector.

questions.q: An electron accelerated from rest through 100 V enters a uniform magnetic field of 2 × 10^-3 T at right angles. Find the radius of its circular path (m = 9.1 × 10^-31 kg, e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C).
questions.explanation: The speed from the accelerating potential gives the radius in the field.

questions.q: Inside a bar magnet the magnetic field lines run from the
options: south pole to the north pole
north pole to the south pole
pole to pole in a random manner
questions.explanation: Outside they go from north to south; they continue inside from south to north to form closed loops.

questions.q: The magnetic susceptibility of a ferromagnetic material is
questions.explanation: Ferromagnets are strongly magnetised, with χ of the order of hundreds or thousands.

questions.q: A magnetic dipole of moment 2 A m² is in a uniform field of 0.5 T. The work done in rotating it from the stable alignment (θ = 0°) to the opposite direction (θ = 180°) is
A long solenoid with 1000 turns per metre carries 1 A and has a core of relative permeability 400. The magnetic field inside is (μ0 = 4π × 10^-7 T m/A)
The axial magnetic field of a short bar magnet at a distance of 0.2 m from its centre is 4 μT. The equatorial field at the same distance is
questions.explanation: The axial field is twice the equatorial field at equal distance, so the equatorial value is 2 μT.

questions.q: Treating the Earth as a dipole of moment 8 × 10^22 A m² and radius 6.4 × 10^6 m, the equatorial surface field B = (μ0/4π)M/r³ is closest to (μ0/4π = 10^-7 T m/A)
Explain why an iron nail is attracted by either pole of a magnet.
questions.answer: The magnet induces magnetisation in the nail so that the end nearer the pole becomes the opposite pole. Opposite poles attract, and the attraction to the near pole is stronger than the repulsion from the far end, so the nail is attracted whichever pole is brought near.
keyPoints: Near end becomes the opposite pole
questions.explanation: A ferromagnet always gets magnetised so as to be attracted.

questions.q: Find the magnetic moment of an electron revolving in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen (the Bohr magneton), using M = eħ/2m with e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C, ħ = 1.055 × 10^-34 J s and m = 9.1 × 10^-31 kg.
keyPoints: M = IA = evr/2 and mvr = ħ so M = eħ/2m
questions.explanation: The orbital moment is tied to the angular momentum L by M = eL/2m.

questions.q: The direction of the induced current in a conductor moving in a magnetic field can be found with
questions.explanation: Fleming's right-hand rule gives the direction of induced current for a moving conductor.

questions.q: Which of the following does not affect the motional emf in a rod moving through a magnetic field?
options: The strength of the magnetic field
questions.explanation: ε = Blv does not involve mass.

questions.q: A coil of 200 turns and area 5 × 10^-3 m² is placed perpendicular to a field that rises uniformly from 0 to 0.8 T in 0.4 s. The induced emf is
Two inductors of 2 mH and 3 mH are connected in series with negligible mutual coupling. The equivalent inductance is
questions.explanation: Inductances in series add: 2 + 3 = 5 mH.

questions.q: A coil of 100 turns and resistance 10 Ω is connected to a galvanometer. The flux through each turn changes by 0.02 Wb. The charge that flows through the circuit is
questions.explanation: q = NΔΦ/R = 100 × 0.02/10 = 0.2 C, independent of the time taken.

questions.q: A 0.2 H coil carries 5 A and the current is switched off in 1 ms. The average induced emf is
State Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction.
questions.answer: First law: whenever the magnetic flux linked with a circuit changes, an emf is induced in it. Second law: the magnitude of the induced emf equals the rate of change of the magnetic flux linked with the circuit (multiplied by the number of turns for a coil).
keyPoints: emf = -N dΦ/dt in magnitude proportional to the rate of change of flux
questions.explanation: The emf exists whether the flux changes by field, area or orientation.

questions.q: A generator coil has 500 turns of area 0.04 m² and rotates at 50 revolutions per second in a field of 0.1 T. Find the peak and rms emf.
questions.answer: Peak emf ≈ 628 V; rms emf ≈ 444 V.
questions.explanation: The rms value is the peak divided by √2.

questions.q: The power factor of an ideal inductor in an AC circuit is
questions.explanation: The phase angle is 90°, so cosφ = 0.

questions.q: An AC ammeter reads
options: the average value over a cycle
questions.explanation: AC meters are calibrated in rms values, which indicate the heating effect.

questions.q: A voltage v = 100 sin ωt is applied across a 50 Ω resistor. The average power dissipated is
The capacitive reactance of a 2 μF capacitor at 50 Hz is closest to
A series LC circuit has L = 1 H and C = 1 μF. Its resonant frequency is closest to
In an ideal LC circuit the maximum charge on the capacitor is 2 μC and C = 1 μF. The total energy of the oscillation is
What is meant by power factor? Why is a low power factor undesirable?
questions.answer: Power factor is cosφ, the ratio of the true power to the apparent power (P = V_rms I_rms cosφ). At a low power factor a larger current is needed to deliver the same power, which increases the I²R loss in the supply lines and the rating of equipment needed.
keyPoints: Low cosφ means larger current and larger line losses
questions.explanation: Only the in-phase part of the current delivers net power.

questions.q: A series circuit has R = 40 Ω, X_L = 100 Ω and X_C = 70 Ω and is connected to a 100 V rms supply. Find the current, the power factor and the average power.
questions.answer: Current = 2 A; power factor = 0.8; average power = 160 W.
questions.explanation: The net reactance is 100 - 70 = 30 Ω (inductive).

questions.q: Which of the following is not an electromagnetic wave?
questions.explanation: Ultrasound is a mechanical (sound) wave and needs a material medium.

questions.q: In an electromagnetic wave the electric and magnetic fields are
options: perpendicular to each other and in phase
perpendicular to each other and 90° out of phase
questions.explanation: E and B are mutually perpendicular, perpendicular to the direction of travel, and reach maxima together.

questions.q: A radio wave of frequency 60 MHz travels in vacuum. Its wavelength is (c = 3 × 10^8 m/s)
The magnetic field amplitude of a plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum is 4 × 10^-8 T. The electric field amplitude is (c = 3 × 10^8 m/s)
A 100 W point source radiates electromagnetic waves uniformly in all directions. Ignoring losses, the intensity at 2 m from it is closest to
A beam of electromagnetic radiation carries 6 × 10^-3 J of energy and is completely absorbed by a surface. The momentum delivered to the surface is (c = 3 × 10^8 m/s)
Explain briefly the greenhouse effect in terms of electromagnetic radiation.
questions.answer: The Earth's surface, warmed by sunlight, emits infrared radiation. Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapour absorb part of this infrared and re-radiate it, including back towards the surface, so the lower atmosphere is warmer than it would otherwise be.
keyPoints: Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit it
Surface and lower atmosphere stay warmer
questions.explanation: Visible sunlight passes in readily, but outgoing infrared is partly trapped.

questions.q: Using μ0 = 4π × 10^-7 T m/A and ε0 = 8.85 × 10^-12 C²/N m², calculate the speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum from c = 1/√(μ0ε0).
questions.explanation: The agreement with the measured speed of light led Maxwell to identify light as an electromagnetic wave.

questions.q: The image formed by a plane mirror is
options: virtual, erect and of the same size as the object
inverted and of the same size
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image the same size as the object, as far behind as the object is in front.

questions.q: A ray of light passing through the optical centre of a thin lens
questions.explanation: Near the optical centre the faces are nearly parallel, so the ray goes straight through.

questions.q: A prism of angle 60° has a minimum deviation of 30°. Its refractive index is
An object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. The magnification of the image is
questions.explanation: The object is at 2f, so the image is at 30 cm on the other side with m = v/u = -1.

questions.q: An object is placed 8 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 12 cm. The image is
options: real, inverted, formed 24 cm in front of the mirror
virtual, erect, formed 24 cm behind the mirror and magnified 3 times
virtual, erect, formed 4.8 cm behind the mirror and diminished
real, inverted, formed 4.8 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = -1/12 + 1/8 = 1/24, so v = +24 cm and m = -v/u = +3, a virtual, erect, enlarged image.

questions.q: A coin lies at the bottom of a beaker. A glass slab of thickness 6 cm and refractive index 1.5 is placed directly on top of the coin. Viewed from above, the coin appears raised by
Find the focal length of a plano-convex lens of refractive index 1.5 whose curved surface has radius of curvature 15 cm.
keyPoints: 1/f = (n - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2) with R1 = 15 cm and R2 = infinity
questions.explanation: The flat face contributes no curvature.

questions.q: A person's near point is 50 cm. What is the power of the lens needed to read comfortably at 25 cm?
questions.answer: +2 D (a convex lens of focal length 50 cm).
keyPoints: The lens must form a virtual image at 50 cm of an object at 25 cm
questions.explanation: This corrects hypermetropia (far-sightedness).

questions.q: In single slit diffraction the central maximum is
options: equal to the other maxima in width and brightness
questions.explanation: The central maximum is twice as wide as the secondary maxima and much brighter.

questions.q: Unpolarised light of intensity I0 passes through an ideal polariser. The transmitted intensity is
questions.explanation: On average half of the intensity is transmitted.

questions.q: In Young's experiment λ = 6000 Å, the slit separation is 0.4 mm and the screen is 1.2 m away. The fringe width is
At the polarising (Brewster) angle, the angle between the reflected and refracted rays is
questions.explanation: At Brewster's angle the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular.

questions.q: Two polaroids are crossed. A third polaroid is inserted between them with its axis at 45° to both. Unpolarised light of intensity I0 falls on the first. The final transmitted intensity is
questions.explanation: After P1: I0/2; after P2: (I0/2)cos²45° = I0/4; after P3 (45° to P2): (I0/4)cos²45° = I0/8.

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment with two equal sources of intensity I0 each, the intensity at a point where the path difference is λ/6 is
questions.explanation: Phase difference = 2π/6 = 60°, so I = 4I0cos²30° = 3I0.

questions.q: State the principle of superposition and the conditions for constructive and destructive interference in terms of path difference.
questions.answer: When two or more waves meet at a point, the resultant displacement is the vector sum of the individual displacements. Interference is constructive when the path difference is nλ (n = 0, 1, 2, ...) and destructive when it is (n + ½)λ.
keyPoints: Resultant displacement is the sum of displacements
questions.explanation: These correspond to phase differences of 2nπ and (2n + 1)π.

questions.q: Two coherent sources have intensities I and 4I. Find the ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity in their interference pattern.
questions.explanation: Maximum and minimum intensities come from the sum and difference of amplitudes.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: The photoelectric saturation current for light above the threshold frequency is proportional to the
questions.explanation: Higher intensity means more photons per second and so more photoelectrons per second.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: For the same speed, which of these has the longest de Broglie wavelength?
questions.explanation: λ = h/mv is greatest for the lightest particle.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: Taking hc = 1240 eV nm, the energy of a photon of wavelength 620 nm is

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: A metal has a work function of 2.65 × 10^-19 J. Its threshold frequency is (h = 6.63 × 10^-34 J s)

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: A metal has work function 2 eV. The ratio of the maximum kinetic energies of photoelectrons for incident photons of 4 eV and 3 eV is
questions.explanation: K1 = 4 - 2 = 2 eV and K2 = 3 - 2 = 1 eV, so the ratio is 2 : 1.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: A proton and an alpha particle are each accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. The ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths λ_p/λ_α is
questions.explanation: λ = h/√(2mqV). With m_α = 4m_p and q_α = 2q_p, λ_p/λ_α = √(4 × 2) = 2√2.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: State de Broglie's hypothesis and write the expression for the wavelength of a particle of mass m and kinetic energy K.
questions.answer: Moving material particles have wave properties; a particle of momentum p has an associated wavelength λ = h/p. In terms of kinetic energy K, p = √(2mK), so λ = h/√(2mK).
questions.explanation: The idea was confirmed by electron diffraction experiments.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: Light of wavelength 400 nm and intensity 1.5 W/m² falls on a photocell surface of area 2 cm². Find the number of photons striking it per second (hc = 1240 eV nm, 1 eV = 1.6 × 10^-19 J). If one photon in 100 ejects an electron, what is the photocurrent?
questions.answer: About 6 × 10^14 photons per second; photocurrent about 0.97 μA (roughly 1 μA).
questions.explanation: The photocurrent equals the charge of the ejected electrons per second.

questions.q: The mass number of a nucleus is equal to the number of
questions.explanation: Mass number A counts the nucleons.

questions.q: In a nuclear reactor the control rods are used to
options: absorb neutrons and control the rate of the reaction
questions.explanation: Rods of cadmium or boron absorb neutrons and so regulate the chain reaction.

questions.q: The speed of the electron in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen is about 2.2 × 10^6 m/s. Its speed in the n = 2 orbit is about
questions.explanation: v_n is proportional to 1/n, so v2 = 2.2 × 10^6/2 = 1.1 × 10^6 m/s.

questions.q: If 1 g of matter were completely converted into energy, the energy released would be (c = 3 × 10^8 m/s)
The density of nuclear matter, compared across different nuclei, is
options: nearly the same for all nuclei
questions.explanation: R = R0A^(1/3) makes volume proportional to A, so mass per unit volume is almost constant (about 2.3 × 10^17 kg/m³).

questions.q: In the hydrogen Lyman series the ratio of the shortest to the longest wavelength is
questions.explanation: 1/λ = R(1 - 1/n²): the longest uses n = 2 (3R/4) and the shortest uses n = ∞ (R), so λmin/λmax = (3R/4)/R = 3/4.

questions.q: What is meant by the binding energy of a nucleus? Why is it released as energy when nucleons combine?
questions.answer: The binding energy is the minimum energy needed to separate a nucleus into its individual protons and neutrons. The mass of a nucleus is less than the sum of the masses of its nucleons; this mass defect Δm is released as energy Δm c² when the nucleons bind together.
keyPoints: Energy needed to separate the nucleus into nucleons
Mass defect Δm = sum of nucleon masses - nuclear mass
questions.explanation: A higher binding energy per nucleon means a more stable nucleus.

questions.q: For the He+ ion (Z = 2), find the radius and the energy of the n = 2 orbit. Take the Bohr radius a0 = 0.53 Å and E_n = -13.6 Z²/n² eV.
questions.explanation: The hydrogen-like formulas scale as 1/Z for radius and Z² for energy.

questions.q: At absolute zero the conductivity of a pure semiconductor is
options: the same as that of a metal
questions.explanation: At 0 K the valence band is full and the conduction band empty, so it behaves as an insulator.

questions.q: The logic gate that is also called an inverter is the
questions.explanation: A NOT gate output is the complement of its single input.

questions.q: The number of diodes used in a full-wave bridge rectifier is
questions.explanation: A bridge rectifier uses four diodes arranged in a bridge.

questions.q: In a transistor the region that is thin and lightly doped is the
questions.explanation: The thin, lightly doped base lets most carriers from the emitter pass on to the collector.

questions.q: In a common-emitter transistor circuit the emitter current is 5.1 mA and the base current is 0.1 mA. The current gain β is
questions.explanation: IC = IE - IB = 5.0 mA, so β = IC/IB = 50.

questions.q: Pure silicon has intrinsic carrier density 1.5 × 10^16 m^-3. It is doped with phosphorus so that the electron density is 10^22 m^-3. The hole density is
Explain the terms depletion region and barrier potential in a p-n junction.
questions.answer: When a p-n junction forms, electrons diffuse from the n-side and holes from the p-side and recombine near the junction, leaving a region with no mobile carriers but with fixed ionised atoms: the depletion region. The fixed charges set up an electric field and a potential difference across the region, the barrier potential, which opposes further diffusion.
keyPoints: Depletion region: layer without mobile charge carriers
It contains immobile positive and negative ions
Barrier potential opposes further diffusion of carriers
questions.explanation: The barrier is about 0.7 V for silicon and 0.3 V for germanium.

questions.q: Each input A and B is passed through a NOT gate and the two results are fed into an AND gate, giving Y = A'B'. Write the truth table and name the equivalent gate.
questions.answer: For (A, B) = (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1) the output Y is 1, 0, 0, 0. This is a NOR gate.
keyPoints: Y is 1 only when both inputs are 0
By De Morgan's law A'B' = (A + B)', a NOR gate
questions.explanation: The output pattern matches that of a NOR gate.
